C0.quote: complexity of determining a winning committee under the Chamberlin–Courant voting rule
C0.note: Winner determination for a multiwinner voting rule (computational aspects).

C1.quote: we show that a simple tweak improves the time complexity to O(nmk)
C1.note: All main results are algorithms, running times and approximation.

C2.1.quote: the list P is referred to as a preference profile

C2.2.quote: Voters rank candidates from best to worst
C2.2.note: Input is linear orders; misrepresentation function rho (consistent with P) is also given as input to the rule, so CARD is included.

C2.3.quote: each voter is assumed to assign a numerical disutility to each candidate
C2.3.note: Preferences and disutilities are described as voters' attributes.

C2.4.quote: takes as input a preference profile P
C2.4.note: Preferences are treated as the input and the rule is applied directly; no statement about submission or reporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.quote: we say that ρ is consistent with P if
C4.1.note: Misrepresentation/dissatisfaction is tied to rankings via consistency (weakly monotone). Not a full utility specification, but a relation to the input is defined. Voter dissatisfaction is used. Applicable since RANK is included. The relation is defined as consistency, which could be SPEC; PART chosen because ρ is an additional given input.

C5.1.quote: Φρ (P, w) measures to what extent the voters are dissatisfied
C5.1.note: Chamberlin–Courant minimizes total voter dissatisfaction (representation); the algorithms optimise it.

C5.2.quote: minimizes Φρ (P, w) among all k-assignment functions for P
C5.2.note: Evaluated on the profile and ρ given as input, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters take no action in the model.

claims.quote: This improvement is significant, as in some of the applications
the performance of our algorithms makes them suitable for a broad range

C9.1.note: Claims about practical applicability (e.g., movie selection, assemblies) and suitability of the rule; claims concern computation more than voter welfare.

C9.2.quote: It has been argued that this rule is well-suited for a variety
C9.2.note: Claims about practical usefulness of results need the assumption that the profile and misrepresentation values reflect held attitudes (and are truthfully obtained); this is not stated.
